prize_parts.citation: For discoveries in the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the development of long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep a single prize part on B025. All six of us place it first and, as the chair's summary notes, each of us says that is not the argument. The argument is the arc: proglucagon processing and the incretin effect (Holst), the pleiotropic biology of GLP-1 and its inactivation by DPP-4 (Drucker), and degradation-resistant, albumin-binding agonists (Knudsen) that lower glycaemia and body weight and reduce cardiovascular events in large independent randomised trials. Maturity is not in question after decades of replication and more than a decade of clinical use. Drucker and Holst are uncontested in all six configurations. I keep Knudsen as the third name because the committee's own framing question has a practical answer: a citation that mentions only hormone biology would not explain why this became a prize-worthy change in medicine, and the acylation strategy is what made a hormone with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly drug. The citation names both physiology and development so that the credit matches what the three people did.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and I do not think the round has resolved it. Four credited names go to three, Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is a real discovery-stage contribution, Habener is outside the credited names, and Knudsen's work was done inside a company, so a reader can say that I am rewarding development over discovery. I cannot verify the priority claims from the supplied credit. If the committee insists on a pure physiology framing, my trio is the less defensible one and Drucker, Holst and Mojsov is the right variant. A single part also leaves out CAR-T and other strong candidates, which is a cost of the three-person limit.

responses.point: Linnarsson keeps Mojsov in the third seat because identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is discovery, and argues the prize should reward what was discovered rather than who built the drug.
responses.response: I take this seriously and it is the strongest version of the opposing case. I have not moved, for two reasons. First, the answer to the chair's question on framing cannot be that the analogue work is only industrial: a clinically useful GLP-1 agonist needed a solution to rapid DPP-4 degradation and renal clearance, which was a mechanistic problem. Second, with Habener outside the credited names, a Mojsov seat gives the committee a priority judgment it cannot fully support from the supplied evidence, whereas Knudsen's contribution is documented and not contested. If the committee settles the priority record in Mojsov's favour, I would consider that variant defensible and would not call it a mistake.

responses.point: Svenningsson, who chairs, argues that long-acting analogue work was itself a biochemical insight about half-life and albumin binding, and in round 1 proposed only June and Sadelain for CAR-T.
responses.response: I agree with the half-life argument and it is the reason I treat Knudsen as discovery rather than product. On CAR-T, my position from round 1 stands: I would not restrict the credit to June and Sadelain without addressing Rosenberg, and I accept that Eshhar's absence from the credited names is a defect no choice among them repairs. In answer to your question about a second part, I do not support one this year. B047 would take at least two of three seats from a trio that is already contested, and the attribution problem would then sit in two parts.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps Mojsov and frames the citation as physiology and the active peptide, so that the prize is about discovery rather than product development, and says optogenetics is a transformative method.
responses.response: On the citation, I think a physiology-only wording leaves a gap the public and the field will see: the therapy that delivered the benefit would be unnamed. On optogenetics, I still rank B038 below the clinical candidates. Its importance as a tool is clear, but the medical consequence is indirect, and six names for three seats would exclude Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, or others, with strong claims. I would not move it into the configuration this round.

responses.point: Sandberg says a prize that leaves out Knudsen could be read as celebrating the therapy while omitting its engineer, and also that a single-achievement prize leaves out CAR-T and optogenetics.
responses.response: I agree with your first point and it is why I stay with the Knudsen trio: the mirror problem applies to the Mojsov trio. On a second part, I think the three-person cap is decisive. A second achievement would leave at most one or two seats for B025, which would drop either Holst or Drucker or both, and I cannot defend that for the strongest, most mature candidate. I therefore keep one part, and I hold B047 and B014 as alternatives and not as additions.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps one part because a second part would shrink the GLP-1 trio, and says that if the committee wants physiology only, the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio would be more defensible.
responses.response: I agree on both points. We have the same configuration and the same condition under which it should be abandoned. I would add that the disclosed condition is a reason for the final ballot to be honest about the framing choice, not a reason to hedge the citation into an unclear compromise.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen should hold the third seat of B025 remains the main open question. I changed nothing from round 1 on it, and priority evidence on Mojsov and Habener that I cannot verify from the supplied credit could change my view.
Whether the committee accepts the acylation and half-life work as discovery, which decides the framing and so the laureate set.

Whether B014 (HPV vaccines) is sufficiently distinct from the earlier HPV-cancer prize, and whether its credited trio is defensible given parallel groups and early deaths, which is why I list it only as an alternative.
Whether Rosenberg belongs in B047 and how Eshhar's absence is handled, which keeps B047 an alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no documented personal or institutional tie to Drucker, Holst, Knudsen, Mojsov or any other credited person on the shortlist, and I do not infer one from shared institutions or topics. My research field is autoimmunity, which touches B047 and B009 only at the margin, and I do not request recusal. No other member has requested one.
